words.sense: very old-fashioned and associated with an earlier era
misconceptions: Anything old has necessarily been replaced by newer equipment

words.sense: no longer used because a modern substitute took its place
misconceptions: A thing becomes obsolete simply by looking old

semantic_axes.description: Old-fashioned appearance or usage differs from being displaced by a newer substitute.

edges.boundary_rule: archaic belongs to an earlier age; obsolete has been superseded by a newer replacement.

misconceptions.M2: Confuses a replacement with mere old-fashioned style
misconceptions.M3: Assumes rare use alone proves either category

chains.frame: Which word best describes the wording in Aisha’s library book?

beats.text: Aisha found expressions in a century-old novel that modern students no longer use in conversation.
beats.decisive_clue: language belongs to an earlier era
beats.reason: The focus is the age and style of words.

beats.text: The book had a bright new cover and clean pages.
beats.decisive_clue: old-fashioned expressions despite a new cover
beats.reason: Physical condition does not modernize historical wording.

chains.feedback_short: Key evidence: old-fashioned expressions despite a new cover.
chains.feedback_deep: archaic means old-fashioned or surviving from an earlier age; obsolete means no longer in use because a newer alternative replaced it. The focus is the age and style of words. Physical condition does not modernize historical wording.
chains.contrast_rule: archaic belongs to an earlier age; obsolete has been superseded by a newer replacement.

hints.attention: Look at the expressions rather than the cover.
hints.axis: Old-fashioned appearance or usage differs from being displaced by a newer substitute.
hints.contrast: archaic belongs to an earlier age; obsolete has been superseded by a newer replacement.
